1	# Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks: Time Horizon Doubling Every 7 Months
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	- URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14499
     5	- Authors: Thomas Kwa, Ben West, Joel Becker, et al. — Model Evaluation & Threat Research (METR)
     6	- Published: March 2025
     7	
     8	## The Time Horizon Metric
     9	
    10	The paper proposes a new metric for quantifying AI autonomous capabilities: the **50% task-completion time horizon** — the duration of tasks (measured by how long they take skilled human professionals) that an AI model can complete with 50% success rate. This provides an intuitive, human-grounded measure of real-world AI capability that allows comparison across vastly different models (e.g., GPT-2 vs. Claude 3.7 Sonnet).
    11	
    12	The methodology involves three steps: (1) assembling a diverse suite of 170 software/research tasks, (2) timing skilled humans and measuring AI agent success rates on these tasks, and (3) fitting a logistic model to estimate the task duration at which each AI agent achieves 50% success.
    13	
    14	![Methodology overview](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    15	
    16	## Task Suite: 170 Tasks from 1 Second to 8 Hours
    17	
    18	The benchmark combines three task suites: HCAST (97 diverse software tasks, 1 min–30 hrs), RE-Bench (7 difficult ML research engineering tasks, all 8 hrs), and Software Atomic Actions / SWAA (66 short single-step tasks, 1 sec–30 sec). Over 800 human baselines totaling 2,529 hours were collected.
    19	
    20	| Family | Human Time | Description |
    21	|---|---|---|
    22	| find_shell_script | 3 seconds | Multiple choice: "Which file is a shell script?" |
    23	| wikipedia_research | 1 minute | Research simple factual information from Wikipedia |
    24	| oxdna_simple | 9 minutes | Detect and fix a bug in molecular dynamics simulation input files |
    25	| munge_data | 56 minutes | Write a Python script to transform JSON data by inferring conversion rules |
    26	| cuda_backtesting | 8 hours | Implement custom CUDA kernels for 30x speedup of a backtesting tool |
    27	
    28	## Exponential Growth in AI Time Horizon (2019–2025)
    29	
    30	The central finding is that the 50% time horizon has grown exponentially from 2019 to 2025, with a **doubling time of approximately 207 days (~7 months)** and an R² of 0.97. Key data points across models:
    31	
    32	| Model | Release Period | 50% Time Horizon |
    33	|---|---|---|
    34	| GPT-2 | 2019 | ~2 seconds |
    35	| GPT-3 (davinci-002) | 2020 | ~9 seconds |
    36	| GPT-3.5-turbo-instruct | 2023 | ~36 seconds |
    37	| GPT-4 (0314) | 2023 | ~5 minutes |
    38	| GPT-4o | 2024 | ~9 minutes |
    39	| Claude 3 Opus | 2024 | ~6 minutes |
    40	| Claude 3.5 Sonnet (New) | 2024 | ~28 minutes |
    41	| o1 | 2024 | ~39 minutes |
    42	| Claude 3.7 Sonnet | 2025 | ~54 minutes |
    43	| o3 | 2025 | ~1 hour 50 minutes |
    44	
    45	![Exponential trend in AI time horizon](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    46	
    47	The 2023–2025 growth rate is approximately 20% faster than the overall 2019–2025 rate, suggesting possible acceleration. The 80% time horizon (tasks completed 80% of the time) shows a similar trend but with horizons roughly 5x shorter.
    48	
    49	![Per-model success probability curves](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
    50	
    51	## Drivers and Limitations
    52	
    53	Progress appears driven by: **improved logical reasoning**, **better tool use**, **greater reliability and self-awareness** in task execution, and **ability to adapt to mistakes**. However, performance is notably lower on less structured, "messier" tasks. External validity remains an open question — the tasks do not perfectly represent the average segment of real-world intellectual labor, though supplementary experiments found little evidence that trends are slower on more realistic tasks.
    54	
    55	## Key Findings
    56	
    57	- **50% time horizon** provides a robust, intuitive metric for tracking AI autonomous capability growth, with R² = 0.97 over 6 years of model releases.
    58	- Frontier AI agents (o3) can now autonomously complete tasks that take skilled humans **nearly 2 hours**, up from 2 seconds for GPT-2 in 2019.
    59	- The doubling time is **~7 months**, with possible acceleration since 2024.
    60	- Naive extrapolation predicts AI will reach a **1-month time horizon (167 work hours) between mid-2028 and mid-2031**, implying automation of many month-long software projects.
    61	- Key capability drivers are reasoning, tool use, and error recovery; key limitations include poor performance on unstructured tasks and uncertain external validity to real-world job distributions.

    10	
    11	## When to Use
    12	
    13	Use when the main artifact is a Microsoft PowerPoint presentation or `.pptx` deck, especially when layouts, templates, placeholders, notes, comments, charts, extraction, editing, or final visual quality matter.
    14	
    15	## Core Rules
    16	
    17	### 1. Choose the workflow before touching the deck
    18	
    19	- Reading text, editing an existing deck, rebuilding from a template, and creating from scratch are different jobs with different failure modes.
    20	- For text extraction or inspection, read the deck before editing it.
    21	- Text extraction plus thumbnail-style visual inspection is safer than editing from shape assumptions alone.
    22	- For template-driven work, inventory the deck before replacing content.
    23	- For deep edits, remember a `.pptx` file is OOXML with separate parts for slides, layouts, masters, media, notes, and comments.
    24	- If a template exists, template fidelity beats generic slide-design instincts.
    25	- Reusing or duplicating a good existing slide is often safer than rebuilding it and hoping the theme still matches.
    26	
    27	### 2. Inventory the deck before replacing content
    28	
    29	- Count the reusable layouts, real placeholders, notes, comments, media, and recurring typography or color patterns first.
    30	- Placeholder indexes and layout indexes are not portable assumptions.
    31	- Inspect the actual slide or template before targeting title, body, chart, or image shapes.
    32	- Speaker notes, comments, and linked assets can live outside the visible slide surface.
    33	- A missing or wrong placeholder target can silently land content in the wrong box or wrong layer.
    34	- Master and layout settings can override local slide edits, so the visible problem is not always on the slide you are editing.
    35	
    36	### 3. Match content to the actual placeholders
    37	
    38	- Count the actual content pieces before choosing a layout.
    39	- Pick layouts based on the real number of ideas, columns, images, or charts the slide needs.
    40	- Do not force two ideas into a three-column slide or cram dense text under a chart.
    41	- Category counts and data series lengths must match or charts will break in ugly ways.
    42	- Explicit sizing beats wishful thinking: text boxes, images, and charts need real space, not "it should fit".
    43	- Do not choose a layout with more placeholders than the content can meaningfully fill.
    44	- Quote layouts are for real quotes, and image-led layouts are for slides that actually have images.
    45	- For chart-, table-, or image-heavy slides, full-slide or two-column layouts are usually safer than stacking dense text above the visual.
    46	
    47	### 4. Preserve the deck's visual language
    48	
    49	- Theme, master, and layout files usually decide fonts, colors, and hierarchy more than any one slide does.
    50	- Start from the deck's actual theme, fonts, spacing, and aspect ratio instead of improvising a new style.
    51	- Reuse the deck's own alignment and spacing system instead of inventing a second visual language.
    52	- Use common fonts for portability and strong contrast for readability.
    53	- Preserve the template's visual logic first; originality matters less than not breaking the deck's existing language.
    54	- Combining slides from multiple sources requires normalizing themes, masters, and alignment afterward.
    55	
    56	### 5. Run content QA and visual QA separately
    57	
    58	- Text overflow, bad alignment, clipped shapes, weak contrast, and placeholder leftovers are normal first-pass failures.
    59	- Run both content QA and visual QA; missing text and broken layout are different failure classes.
    60	- Render or inspect the actual deck output before delivery when layout matters.
    61	- Search for leftover template junk, sample labels, and placeholder text before calling the deck finished.
    62	- Check notes, comments, labels, legends, and chart/table semantics separately from the visual pass.
    63	- A deck can pass text extraction and still fail on overlap, clipping, wrong theme inheritance, or broken notes.
    64	- Thumbnail grids and rendered slides usually reveal layout bugs faster than code or text inspection.
    65	- Assume the first render is wrong and do at least one fix-and-verify cycle before calling the deck finished.
    66	- Re-check affected slides after each fix because one spacing change often creates another issue.
    67	
    68	### 6. Keep decks portable and review-safe
    69	
    70	- Template masters can override direct edits in surprising ways.
    71	- Complex effects may degrade across PowerPoint, LibreOffice, and conversion pipelines, so keep important content robust without them.
    72	- Image sizing, font substitution, and placeholder mismatch are common reasons a deck looks good in code and bad on screen.
    73	- Notes, comments, linked media, and merged decks can stay broken even when the visible slide looks fine.
    74	
    75	## Common Traps
    76	
    77	- Placeholder text and sample charts often survive template reuse if not explicitly replaced.
    78	- Directly editing one slide can fail if the real issue lives in the master or layout.
    79	- Charts, icons, and text boxes need enough space; near-collisions are usually visible only after rendering.
    80	- Layout indexes vary by template, so built-in assumptions from one deck often break in another.
    81	- A missing placeholder or wrong shape target can silently put content in the wrong place.
    82	- Counting the text ideas after choosing the layout usually leads to empty placeholders, weak hierarchy, or leftover template junk.
    83	- Font substitution can move line breaks and wreck careful spacing.
    84	- Speaker notes, comments, and linked media can stay broken even when the visible slide looks fine.
    85	- A deck can pass text inspection and still fail visually because of overlap, contrast, or edge clipping.
    86	- Editing from one slide alone can miss the real source of truth in the theme, master, or layout definitions.
    87	- Choosing a quote, comparison, or multi-column layout without matching content usually makes the deck look templated rather than intentional.
    88	- Combining or duplicating slides without checking masters and themes can create subtle inconsistency slide by slide.
    89	- Aspect-ratio mismatches like `16:9` versus `4:3` can shift every placement decision even when each slide looks locally reasonable.
    90	
    91	## Related Skills
    92	Install with `clawhub install <slug>` if user confirms:
    93	- `documents` — Document workflows that often feed presentation content.
    94	- `design` — Visual direction and layout decisions.
    95	- `brief` — Concise business messaging for slide narratives.
    96	
    97	## Feedback
    98	
    99	- If useful: `clawhub star powerpoint-pptx`
   100	- Stay updated: `clawhub sync`

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Build an 8-slide 16:9 analytical presentation using python-pptx.
Follows the powerpoint-pptx skill workflow: data-forward, technical tone,
structured layouts, and visual QA.
"""

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.dml.color import RgbColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.oxml.ns import nsmap
from pptx.oxml import parse_xml
import os

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
OUTPUT_PATH = "/app/output/final_deck.pptx"
ASSETS_DIR = "/app/benchmark/assets"
SLIDE_WIDTH = Inches(13.333)
SLIDE_HEIGHT = Inches(7.5)

# Color palette — dark, analytical, data-forward
DARK_BG = RgbColor(0x12, 0x18, 0x2B)       # deep navy background
ACCENT = RgbColor(0x3A, 0xB7, 0xF7)        # bright blue accent
TEXT_WHITE = RgbColor(0xF5, 0xF5, 0xF5)    # off-white primary text
TEXT_GRAY = RgbColor(0xA0, 0xA8, 0xB8)     # muted gray secondary text
GRID_LINE = RgbColor(0x2A, 0x32, 0x45)     # subtle grid/border
HIGHLIGHT = RgbColor(0xF4, 0xB4, 0x00)     # amber highlight for key stats

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def set_slide_bg(slide, color):
    """Set solid background color for a slide."""
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color


def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size, font_color,
                bold=False, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri"):
    """Add a text box with specified formatting."""
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = font_size
    p.font.color.rgb = font_color
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    return tf


def add_bullet_text(slide, left, top, width, height, bullets, font_size,
                    font_color, bullet_color=None, font_name="Calibri", line_spacing=1.3):
    """Add a text box with multiple bullet paragraphs."""
    if bullet_color is None:
        bullet_color = font_color
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, txt in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = txt
        p.font.size = font_size
        p.font.color.rgb = font_color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.space_after = Pt(10)
        p.line_spacing = line_spacing
        p.level = 0
    return tf


def add_horizontal_line(slide, left, top, width, color, thickness=Pt(1)):
    """Add a thin horizontal line shape."""
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(
        MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, thickness
    )
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape


def add_figure(slide, img_path, left, top, width, height):
    """Add an image to the slide if it exists."""
    if os.path.exists(img_path):
        slide.shapes.add_picture(img_path, left, top, width=width, height=height)
    else:
        # placeholder red box if missing
        shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
        shape.fill.solid()
        shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = RgbColor(0xFF, 0x00, 0x00)
        shape.line.fill.background()
        tf = shape.text_frame
        tf.paragraphs[0].text = "[Image not found]"
        tf.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = TEXT_WHITE


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Slide builders
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_title_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])  # blank
    set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)

    # Accent top bar
    slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0), Inches(0),
                           SLIDE_WIDTH, Pt(6)).fill.solid().fore_color.rgb = ACCENT

    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.8), Inches(2.0), Inches(11.7), Inches(1.2),
                "Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks",
                Pt(44), TEXT_WHITE, bold=True, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    # Subtitle / headline finding
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.8), Inches(3.3), Inches(11.7), Inches(0.8),
                "Time Horizon Doubling Every ~7 Months",
                Pt(28), ACCENT, bold=True, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    # Key stat box
    stat_box = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE,
                                      Inches(0.8), Inches(4.4), Inches(7.5), Inches(1.1))
    stat_box.fill.solid()
    stat_box.fill.fore_color.rgb = RgbColor(0x1E, 0x27, 0x3A)
    stat_box.line.color.rgb = ACCENT
    stat_tf = stat_box.text_frame
    stat_tf.word_wrap = True
    p = stat_tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = "Headline finding: The 50% task-completion time horizon for frontier AI agents has doubled roughly every 7 months since 2019, rising from ~2 seconds (GPT-2) to ~1 hour 50 minutes (o3)."
    p.font.size = Pt(16)
    p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_GRAY
    p.font.name = "Calibri"

    # Source / authors
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.8), Inches(6.4), Inches(11.7), Inches(0.5),
                "Kwa, West, Becker, et al. — METR  |  arXiv:2503.14499  |  March 2025",
                Pt(14), TEXT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    return slide


def build_metric_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)

    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.7),
                "A New Metric: 50% Task-Completion Time Horizon",
                Pt(32), TEXT_WHITE, bold=True)

    add_horizontal_line(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.05), Inches(12.0), ACCENT, Pt(2))

    # Three-step flow
    steps = [
        ("1", "Assemble diverse task suite",
         "Curate 170 software / research tasks spanning 1 second to 8 hours of skilled human effort."),
        ("2", "Measure humans & AI agents",
         "Time skilled human professionals on each task; run AI agents and record success rates."),
        ("3", "Fit logistic model",
         "Estimate the task duration at which the AI achieves 50% success — the time horizon."),
    ]

    box_w = Inches(3.7)
    box_h = Inches(2.0)
    start_x = Inches(0.6)
    y = Inches(1.4)
    gap = Inches(0.35)

    for i, (num, title, desc) in enumerate(steps):
        x = start_x + i * (box_w + gap)
        # card background
        card = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, x, y, box_w, box_h)
        card.fill.solid()
        card.fill.fore_color.rgb = RgbColor(0x1E, 0x27, 0x3A)
        card.line.color.rgb = GRID_LINE

        # number circle
        circ = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, x + Inches(0.15), y + Inches(0.15),
                                      Inches(0.45), Inches(0.45))
        circ.fill.solid()
        circ.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT
        circ.line.fill.background()
        circ_tf = circ.text_frame
        circ_tf.paragraphs[0].text = num
        circ_tf.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(18)
        circ_tf.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
        circ_tf.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = DARK_BG
        circ_tf.paragraphs[0].alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER

        # title
        add_textbox(slide, x + Inches(0.7), y + Inches(0.18), box_w - Inches(0.9), Inches(0.4),
                    title, Pt(16), TEXT_WHITE, bold=True)
        # desc
        add_textbox(slide, x + Inches(0.15), y + Inches(0.7), box_w - Inches(0.3), Inches(1.2),
                    desc, Pt(14), TEXT_GRAY)

    # Methodology figure
    fig_path = os.path.join(ASSETS_DIR, "figure_2.jpg")
    add_figure(slide, fig_path, Inches(0.6), Inches(3.7), Inches(12.0), Inches(3.4))

    # Caption
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(7.05), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.3),
                "Figure: Methodology overview — task suite construction, human baseline timing, and logistic model fitting.",
                Pt(12), TEXT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

    return slide


def build_task_suite_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)

    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.7),
                "170 Tasks Spanning 3 Seconds to 8 Hours of Human Effort",
                Pt(32), TEXT_WHITE, bold=True)
    add_horizontal_line(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.05), Inches(12.0), ACCENT, Pt(2))

    # Table: task suite composition
    rows, cols = 4, 4
    table_left = Inches(0.6)
    table_top = Inches(1.3)
    table_width = Inches(12.0)
    table_height = Inches(1.8)
    table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, table_left, table_top, table_width, table_height).table

    # Column widths
    table.columns[0].width = Inches(3.0)
    table.columns[1].width = Inches(2.5)
    table.columns[2].width = Inches(3.5)
    table.columns[3].width = Inches(3.0)

    headers = ["Suite", "Tasks", "Human Time Range", "Description"]
    data = [
        ["HCAST", "97", "1 min – 30 hrs", "Diverse software engineering tasks (debugging, refactoring, data munging)."],
        ["RE-Bench", "7", "~8 hrs each", "Difficult ML research engineering tasks (e.g., custom CUDA kernels)."],
        ["SWAA", "66", "1 sec – 30 sec", "Short single-step atomic actions (e.g., identify shell scripts)."],
    ]

    def style_cell(cell, text, font_size, font_color, bold=False, bg_color=None):
        cell.text = text
        for paragraph in cell.text_frame.paragraphs:
            paragraph.font.size = font_size
            paragraph.font.color.rgb = font_color
            paragraph.font.bold = bold
            paragraph.font.name = "Calibri"
        if bg_color:
            cell.fill.solid()
            cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = bg_color

    header_bg = RgbColor(0x1E, 0x27, 0x3A)
    for c, h in enumerate(headers):
        style_cell(table.cell(0, c), h, Pt(15), TEXT_WHITE, bold=True, bg_color=header_bg)

    for r, row_data in enumerate(data, start=1):
        for c, val in enumerate(row_data):
            style_cell(table.cell(r, c), val, Pt(14), TEXT_GRAY)

    # Example tasks table (smaller, below)
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(3.3), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.4),
                "Example Tasks by Human Duration", Pt(18), TEXT_WHITE, bold=True)

    rows2, cols2 = 6, 3
    table2 = slide.shapes.add_table(rows2, cols2, table_left, Inches(3.7), table_width, Inches(2.4)).table
    table2.columns[0].width = Inches(3.5)
    table2.columns[1].width = Inches(2.5)
    table2.columns[2].width = Inches(6.0)

    headers2 = ["Task Family", "Human Time", "Description"]
    data2 = [
        ["find_shell_script", "3 seconds", "Multiple choice: Which file is a shell script?"],
        ["wikipedia_research", "1 minute", "Research simple factual information from Wikipedia."],
        ["oxdna_simple", "9 minutes", "Detect and fix a bug in molecular dynamics simulation input files."],
        ["munge_data", "56 minutes", "Write a Python script to transform JSON data by inferring conversion rules."],
        ["cuda_backtesting", "8 hours", "Implement custom CUDA kernels for 30× speedup of a backtesting tool."],
    ]

    for c, h in enumerate(headers2):
        style_cell(table2.cell(0, c), h, Pt(14), TEXT_WHITE, bold=True, bg_color=header_bg)
    for r, row_data in enumerate(data2, start=1):
        for c, val in enumerate(row_data):
            style_cell(table2.cell(r, c), val, Pt(13), TEXT_GRAY)

    # Baseline note
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(6.25), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.3),
                "Over 800 human baselines collected (2,529 total hours).",
                Pt(12), TEXT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    return slide


def build_exponential_trend_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)

    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.35), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.7),
                "AI Task Horizon Grew from 2 Seconds (GPT-2) to ~1 Hour 50 Minutes (o3) in 6 Years",
                Pt(30), TEXT_WHITE, bold=True)
    add_horizontal_line(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.0), Inches(12.0), ACCENT, Pt(2))

    # Key stats row
    stats = [
        ("~207 days", "Doubling time"),
        ("R² = 0.97", "Fit quality"),
        ("~7 months", "Period"),
    ]
    stat_w = Inches(3.5)
    stat_h = Inches(0.6)
    stat_y = Inches(1.15)
    stat_start_x = Inches(0.6)
    gap = Inches(0.5)
    for i, (val, lbl) in enumerate(stats):
        x = stat_start_x + i * (stat_w + gap)
        box = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, x, stat_y, stat_w, stat_h)
        box.fill.solid()
        box.fill.fore_color.rgb = RgbColor(0x1E, 0x27, 0x3A)
        box.line.color.rgb = ACCENT
        tf = box.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = f"{val}  —  {lbl}"
        p.font.size = Pt(16)
        p.font.color.rgb = HIGHLIGHT
        p.font.bold = True
        p.font.name = "Calibri"
        p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER

    # Main figure
    fig_path = os.path.join(ASSETS_DIR, "figure_1.jpg")
    add_figure(slide, fig_path, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.95), Inches(12.0), Inches(4.8))

    # Caption
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(6.85), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.3),
                "Figure: Exponential trend in 50% time horizon vs. model release date. Key milestones: GPT-2 (~2 sec), GPT-4 (~5 min), o3 (~1 hr 50 min).",
                Pt(12), TEXT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

    return slide


def build_success_curves_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)

    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.35), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.7),
                "Success Probability Drops Sharply as Task Length Increases for All Models",
                Pt(30), TEXT_WHITE, bold=True)
    add_horizontal_line(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.0), Inches(12.0), ACCENT, Pt(2))

    # Figure
    fig_path = os.path.join(ASSETS_DIR, "figure_3.jpg")
    add_figure(slide, fig_path, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.2), Inches(12.0), Inches(5.5))

    # Caption / annotation
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(6.85), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.4),
                "Figure: Per-model success probability curves. Frontier models (Claude 3.7 Sonnet, o3) push the curve rightward; older models (GPT-2, GPT-3) drop to near-zero within seconds.",
                Pt(12), TEXT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

    return slide


def build_drivers_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)

    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.7),
                "Reasoning, Tool Use, and Error Recovery Drive Time Horizon Growth",
                Pt(32), TEXT_WHITE, bold=True)
    add_horizontal_line(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.05), Inches(12.0), ACCENT, Pt(2))

    # Two-column layout
    col_w = Inches(5.8)
    left_x = Inches(0.6)
    right_x = Inches(6.9)
    y = Inches(1.3)

    # Left: Drivers
    add_textbox(slide, left_x, y, col_w, Inches(0.4), "Key Capability Drivers", Pt(20), ACCENT, bold=True)
    drivers = [
        "• Improved logical reasoning — longer chains of inference without degradation.",
        "• Better tool use — effective integration of IDEs, terminals, libraries, and APIs.",
        "• Greater reliability & self-awareness — knowing when to stop, verify, or ask.",
        "• Ability to adapt to mistakes — detecting errors and backtracking autonomously.",
    ]
    add_bullet_text(slide, left_x, y + Inches(0.45), col_w, Inches(3.0), drivers, Pt(16), TEXT_GRAY)

    # Right: Limitations
    add_textbox(slide, right_x, y, col_w, Inches(0.4), "Limitations & Open Questions", Pt(20), HIGHLIGHT, bold=True)
    limits = [
        "• Performance is notably lower on less structured, “messier” tasks.",
        "• External validity remains uncertain — tasks may not perfectly represent real-world intellectual labor.",
        "• Supplementary experiments found little evidence that trends are slower on more realistic tasks, but further validation is needed.",
    ]
    add_bullet_text(slide, right_x, y + Inches(0.45), col_w, Inches(3.0), limits, Pt(16), TEXT_GRAY)

    # Bottom insight box
    box = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, Inches(0.6), Inches(5.0), Inches(12.0), Inches(1.3))
    box.fill.solid()
    box.fill.fore_color.rgb = RgbColor(0x1E, 0x27, 0x3A)
    box.line.color.rgb = ACCENT
    tf = box.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = "Insight: The gap between structured benchmark tasks and messy real-world work is the critical unknown. Closing it could accelerate—or complicate—forecasts."
    p.font.size = Pt(16)
    p.font.color.rgb = TEXT_WHITE
    p.font.name = "Calibri"
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT

    return slide


def build_extrapolation_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)

    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.7),
                "Extrapolation Predicts Month-Long Task Automation by 2028–2031",
                Pt(32), TEXT_WHITE, bold=True)
    add_horizontal_line(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.05), Inches(12.0), ACCENT, Pt(2))

    # Big forecast number
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.3), Inches(6.0), Inches(0.8),
                "1 month time horizon", Pt(36), HIGHLIGHT, bold=True)
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(2.0), Inches(6.0), Inches(0.5),
                "≈ 167 work hours  |  mid-2028 to mid-2031", Pt(18), TEXT_GRAY)

    # Supporting bullets
    bullets = [
        "• Naive exponential extrapolation of the 2019–2025 trend reaches >1 month horizon between mid-2028 and mid-2031.",
        "• The 2023–2025 growth rate is ~20% faster than the overall 6-year rate, suggesting possible acceleration.",
        "• 80% time horizon follows a similar trend but is roughly 5× shorter than the 50% horizon.",
        "• Caveats: external validity uncertain; trend may bend due to data scarcity, compute limits, or algorithmic plateaus.",
    ]
    add_bullet_text(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(2.6), Inches(12.0), Inches(3.2), bullets, Pt(16), TEXT_GRAY)

    # Bottom timeline visual (simple bar with markers)
    bar_y = Inches(6.0)
    bar_w = Inches(11.0)
    bar_h = Pt(12)
    bar_x = Inches(0.8)
    slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, bar_x, bar_y, bar_w, bar_h).fill.solid().fore_color.rgb = GRID_LINE

    markers = [
        (Inches(0.8), "2019\nGPT-2\n2 sec"),
        (Inches(3.5), "2023\nGPT-4\n5 min"),
        (Inches(6.2), "2025\no3\n1h 50m"),
        (Inches(9.5), "2028–31\n?\n1 month"),
    ]
    for mx, mtext in markers:
        # dot
        dot = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, mx - Pt(6), bar_y - Pt(5), Pt(12), Pt(12))
        dot.fill.solid()
        dot.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT
        dot.line.fill.background()
        # label
        add_textbox(slide, mx - Inches(0.5), bar_y + Inches(0.2), Inches(1.0), Inches(0.6),
                    mtext, Pt(11), TEXT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

    return slide


def build_takeaways_slide(prs):
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
    set_slide_bg(slide, DARK_BG)

    # Title
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.7),
                "Takeaways: Exponential Autonomous Capability Growth Demands Proactive Safety Governance",
                Pt(30), TEXT_WHITE, bold=True)
    add_horizontal_line(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.05), Inches(12.0), ACCENT, Pt(2))

    takeaways = [
        "1. Robust metric — The 50% time horizon is an intuitive, human-grounded measure of AI autonomy with R² = 0.97 over 6 years of releases.",
        "2. Rapid doubling — The horizon doubles every ~7 months; the 2023–2025 rate is ~20% faster, hinting at acceleration.",
        "3. Current frontier — o3 autonomously completes tasks requiring nearly 2 hours of skilled human work, up from 2 seconds for GPT-2.",
        "4. External validity open — Benchmark tasks may not perfectly represent real-world intellectual labor; generalization remains uncertain.",
        "5. Governance imperative — If trends hold, month-long software project automation arrives by 2028–2031. Safety frameworks, monitoring, and policy must outpace capability growth.",
    ]

    add_bullet_text(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.25), Inches(12.0), Inches(5.0), takeaways, Pt(17), TEXT_GRAY)

    # Footer accent
    add_horizontal_line(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(6.9), Inches(12.0), ACCENT, Pt(1))
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.6), Inches(7.0), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.3),
                "Kwa, West, Becker, et al. — METR  |  arXiv:2503.14499  |  March 2025",
                Pt(12), TEXT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    return slide


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def main():
    prs = Presentation()
    prs.slide_width = SLIDE_WIDTH
    prs.slide_height = SLIDE_HEIGHT

    build_title_slide(prs)
    build_metric_slide(prs)
    build_task_suite_slide(prs)
    build_exponential_trend_slide(prs)
    build_success_curves_slide(prs)
    build_drivers_slide(prs)
    build_extrapolation_slide(prs)
    build_takeaways_slide(prs)

    prs.save(OUTPUT_PATH)
    print(f"Saved deck to {OUTPUT_PATH}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The 8-slide presentation has been built and saved to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx`. It follows the structural outline from `task_input.json`, uses only data from `source_brief.md`, and adheres to the `powerpoint-pptx` skill workflow. Key details:
